items.title: hover is not RICH on generic parameters and their constraints: `Flow` in `fun switch<U, I: Flow<U>>`; `F`, `Flow` and `T` in `impl type F: Flow<type T>`; `T` in `fun sub(own self, observer: \|T\| void)`
items.discussion: the owner (2026-10-01); E237/E238/E239 (the hover arc, Order 45's editor-45)
items.body: Expected: a trait named in a bound hovers as the trait (its header, doc and required members, as E237 does for a trait-typed value); a type parameter hovers as a type parameter — its name, its bounds, and where it is declared (`type T` of `impl type F: Flow<type T>`, or `U` of `fun switch<U, ..>`) — at the declaration AND at every use (a closure type's `T`, a parameter type, a return type). Pins per shape in the title. Sizing S–M; editor lane.

items.title: hover is WRONG on a match case's pattern: `None` in `match x { None => {}, _ => {} }`
items.discussion: the owner (2026-10-01); E240, the hover arc (E237–E239)
items.body: Expected: a variant pattern hovers as the variant of the SCRUTINEE's type with its type arguments substituted (`Option<i32>::None`, a payload variant with its fields), with the variant's doc; a binding inside a pattern hovers as a binding with its type. Reproduce first and record what is shown today (the item does not say); check the sibling shapes: `Some(v)`, a struct-variant pattern, a qualified `Option::None`, a literal and `_`. Sizing S; editor lane.
